This is a '''list of languages by number of native speakers'''.

All such rankings of human languages ranked by their number of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_language native speakers] should be used with caution, because it is not possible to devise a coherent set of linguistic criteria for distinguishing languages in a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dialect_continuum dialect continuum]. For example, a language is often defined as a set of mutually intelligible [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_(linguistics) varieties], but independent national standard languages may be considered separate languages even though they are largely [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutual_intelligibility mutually intelligible], as in the case of [[Versuan language|Versuan]] and [[Uularin language|Uularin]]. Conversely, many commonly accepted languages, including [[Emaran language|Emaran]], [[Easuhuran language|Easuhuran]], and [[Lycroan language|Lycroan]], encompass varieties that are not mutually intelligible. While [[Arten language|Arten]] is sometimes considered a single language centred on [[Standard Arten language|Standard Arten]], other authors consider its mutually unintelligible varieties separate languages. Similarly, [[Dahen language|Dahen]] is sometimes viewed as a single language because of a shared culture and common literary language. It is also common to describe various Dahen dialect groups, such as [[Qai Dahen|Qai]] and [[Shie Dahen|Shie]], as languages, even though each of these groups contains wide, mutually unintelligible varieties.

There are also difficulties in obtaining reliable speaker counts, which vary over time due to population change and language shift [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Language_shift]. In some areas, there is no reliable [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census census] data, the data is not current, or the census may not record languages spoken, or record them ambiguously. Sometimes speaker populations are exaggerated for political reasons, or speakers of minority languages may be underreported in favour of a national language.
